about: Tier B of the release gate (scripts/e2e-gate.sh agent). A real build of a brief that BOSS built on shared-server in September 2026 in 13.7 min (run crun_b6195190): the smallest of the three reference builds. Started on the direct code-task path (POST /v1/code-tasks), on top of the deterministic full-stack web scaffold that brief was built on.
preamble:
A buildable FULL-STACK scaffold ALREADY EXISTS on this branch. Do NOT re-init the project, change the stack, or edit the config/build files.

FRONTEND: Vite + React + TypeScript + Tailwind + shadcn-style — index.html, src/main.tsx, src/App.tsx (a working example, replace it), src/index.css (design tokens), src/lib/utils.ts (cn), src/components/ui/button.tsx + card.tsx.
BACKEND: server/index.js (Express: serves the built frontend AND /api from ONE process), server/db.js (better-sqlite3, migrate() + idempotent seed()), server/migrations/001_init.sql. `npm start` runs the whole app; `npm run dev` runs both halves; `npm run verify` = typecheck + build + end-to-end tests.

THE BACKEND IS NOT OPTIONAL. If the app stores ANYTHING — records, requests, submissions, state a user expects to still be there tomorrow — it goes in the database through the server. Extend the worked example: rename the `items` table to your domain in a NEW migration, add the routes it needs, and have the React code call them with fetch. Do NOT keep application data in useState and do NOT use localStorage as the store.

Why this is stated so plainly: an expense-approval app was built here whose approvals vanished when the tab closed. It looked complete and was not. Data that does not survive a page reload is the single most common way these builds fail.

Build the feature in a FEW focused files: types/logic under src/lib/, presentational pieces under src/components/, API routes in server/, and WIRE it into src/App.tsx. `npm run verify` MUST pass.

VISUAL DESIGN — match the brand's PERSONALITY, do not default to plain corporate:
• You MAY (and for a creative/portfolio/design/events/food/kids brand you SHOULD) RETHEME the palette by editing the design tokens in src/index.css — change --accent and add extra vivid accent hues, and use rich gradients (bg-gradient-to-*), not one flat blue. For a design studio / portfolio go BOLD and colorful (multi-hue gradients, vibrant sections, large expressive type); for finance/enterprise stay restrained. Read the domain and choose.
• Add a distinctive Google Font via a <link> in index.html (e.g. a display font for headings + a clean body font) and set it in the Tailwind/CSS theme.
• Add tasteful motion: CSS transitions on hover, subtle keyframe/scroll reveals, card lift shadows. Generous spacing, rounded corners, strong visual hierarchy.
IMAGERY — never ship empty flat sections. Use real placeholder images (NO API key needed):
• https://picsum.photos/seed/<word>/<w>/<h> (reliable) or https://source.unsplash.com/<w>x<h>/?<keywords> for heroes, galleries, cards. For a portfolio, build an image GRID/masonry of these. Leave a clear code comment where the owner swaps in their real photos.
INTEGRATIONS (wire only if the app needs them):
• PAYMENTS (Stripe): add a 'Buy / Book / Pay' button that opens a Stripe Payment Link — put the URL in a clearly-marked config const (e.g. STRIPE_PAYMENT_LINK = 'https://buy.stripe.com/test_XXXX') for the owner to replace. NO backend needed. (Only if a real cart/dynamic price is required, note that a serverless checkout endpoint would be a follow-up.)
• DATABASE / PERSISTENCE: use the SQLite database already on this branch, through the server. It needs no keys, no signup and no configuration, and it works the moment the app starts. Add a migration for your tables, and routes that read and write them.

# Onboarding Path Builder – Product Requirements Document (PRD)

*Version:* 1.0 – **April 2026**  
*Authors:* Facilitator / Chief of Staff (synthesis), Product Manager, Engineering Lead, UX Lead, Privacy Lead, Security Lead  
*Stakeholders:* Buddy (author) team, New‑joiner (trainee) team, Engineering Ops, Finance  

---  

## 1. Summary
A **lightweight, command‑verified onboarding path builder** that lets a buddy author role‑specific “golden paths” (read → run → ship) and automatically tracks progress, flags steps that repeatedly fail, and surfaces aggregate health to the buddy without exposing personal data. The product ships as a **hosted SaaS** with an **embeddable iframe** for integration into existing platforms (Backstage, Cortex, etc.).

> **Done** when a step’s checkpoint command fails, the failure is reported to the buddy dashboard, and the system flags any step that exceeds the rot‑detection thresholds.

---  

## 2. Problem & Context
| Problem | Why it matters | Evidence (research) |
|---------|----------------|----------------------|
| **“It works on my machine”** failures delay first commit. | ≈ 30 % of time‑to‑first‑commit (TTFC) is spent troubleshooting environment set‑up. | Adaptavist blog – “Why time‑to‑first‑commit is the business metric you’re not tracking”. |
| **Repeated Zoom walkthroughs** waste buddy time. | Average 30 min per hire on manual walkthroughs. | BetterWithData Substack – “Improving onboarding”. |
| **Stale documentation** silently breaks paths. | Undetected failures generate support tickets; no built‑in rot detection in existing tools. | Port pricing page – “golden paths” lack automated failure detection. |
| **Lack of visibility** without surveillance. | Managers need aggregate health, not per‑person spying. | GDPR‑compliant design principle; privacy research. |
| **Market gap** for a **stand‑alone** yet **embeddable** path builder that runs real commands (no checklist‑only tools). | Competitors (Port, Cortex, Backstage) either require heavy platform integration or offer only checklist UI. | Competitor analysis (Port, Cortex, Backstage, Trainual/Whatfix). |

---  

## 3. Goals & Non‑Goals
### Goals
| Metric | Target | Rationale |
|--------|--------|-----------|
| **Time‑to‑first‑commit (TTFC)** reduction | ≥ 30 % (10 days → ≤ 7 days) | Directly tied to command‑verified steps. |
| **Buddy time saved** per hire | ≥ 30 min | Replaces manual walkthroughs. |
| **Rot detection accuracy** | Flag steps with ≥ 20 % failure across ≥ 5 users in 48 h (configurable) | Early signal for stale docs. |
| **Adoption** | 150 active paths in first 6 months (mixed roles) | Demonstrates market need. |
| **SLA** | 99.5 % availability, < 1 s status latency | Real‑time progress essential. |

### Non‑Goals (out of scope for MVP)
- AI‑generated onboarding steps (future flag only).  
- Full‑blown LMS features (e.g., quizzes, certificates).  
- Deep analytics beyond aggregate failure percentages (e.g., per‑user error logs).  
- Multi‑region data residency (initially US‑EU single region).  

---  

## 4. Target Users
| Persona | Primary Needs |
|---------|---------------|
| **Buddy / Path Author** (senior engineer, designer lead) | Create reusable, role‑specific paths; see where newcomers get stuck; avoid repetitive walkthroughs. |
| **New Joiner** (developer, designer, product) | Follow a clear, ordered list of real tasks; see progress; get immediate feedback when a command fails. |
| **Team Lead / Manager** | High‑level health of onboarding across the team without per‑person monitoring. |
| **Ops / Security** | Secure sandbox execution, audit‑ready logs, privacy‑compliant data retention. |

---  

## 5. Requirements  

### 5.1 Functional Requirements
| ID | Requirement | Description | Owner |
|----|-------------|-------------|-------|
| **F‑1** | Ordered steps with command‑verified checkpoint | Each step stores a shell command; a sandbox runs it, success = exit 0. | PM / Eng |
| **F‑2** | Step types: **Read**, **Run**, **Ship** | “Read” displays markdown; “Run” executes a command; “Ship” requires opening a PR (creates a GitHub PR via API). | PM |
| **F‑3** | Per‑role path templates | Author selects target role(s); joiner sees only steps for their role. | PM |
| **F‑4** | Dual‑side progress view | Joiner sees “Step X of Y – ✅/❌”; Buddy sees aggregate bar + failure heat‑map. | UX |
| **F‑5** | Rot‑detection engine | Nightly job evaluates failures; flags steps surpassing configurable thresholds. | Eng |
| **F‑6** | Path editor UI | Drag‑and‑drop + keyboard reordering, OS selector, network whitelist, copy‑command button. | UX / Eng |
| **F‑7** | Light‑weight sandbox agent | Binary (≈ 3 MB) with Docker fallback; runs in isolated container (Firecracker/OCI). | Eng |
| **F‑8** | Buddy dashboard “Stale Step” badge | Badge appears on step tile; clicking opens detail view with failure % and recent logs (scrubbed). | UX |
| **F‑9** | Sample data seed | On first launch, a “Web App Backend” path with 5 steps is pre‑populated. | Eng |
| **F‑10** | Confirmable destructive actions | Deleting a path or step triggers modal; undo via “Trash → Restore” within 30 days. | UX |

### 5.2 Non‑Functional Requirements
| ID | Requirement | Acceptance Metric | Owner |
|----|-------------|-------------------|-------|
| **N‑1** | Security sandbox | No outbound network except whitelisted; seccomp profile enforced; penetration test pass. | Security |
| **N‑2** | Privacy‑by‑design data model | Store only `user_sub`, `path_id`, `step_id`, `outcome`, `timestamp`; stdout/stderr scrubbed; 90‑day retention; purge on HR termination. | Privacy |
| **N‑3** | Accessibility (WCAG AA) | aXe automated scan = 0 violations; manual keyboard test passes. | UX |
| **N‑4** | Performance (real‑time) | Status push ≤ 800 ms after command finishes (WebSocket). | Eng |
| **N‑5** | Reliability | Autoscaling pool; 99.5 % uptime SLA; < 2 % error under 500 concurrent users load test. | Eng |
| **N‑6** | Responsiveness | Layout works from 360 px to 1920 px; no horizontal scroll. | UX |
| **N‑7** | Visual language consistency | One type‑scale, spacing rhythm, single accent color across all screens. | UX |
| **N‑8** | Observability | OpenTelemetry → Prometheus → Grafana; dashboards for step‑failure ≤ 5 % and avg‑TTFC. | Eng |
| **N‑9** | Billing‑ready usage tracking | Anonymous hashed user IDs; per‑active‑path and per‑seat counters stored. | PM |

---  

## 6. Proposed Solution  

### 6.1 High‑level Architecture
```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph Frontend
        FE[Web UI (React + Tailwind)]
        FE -->|HTTPS| API[API Gateway (JWT auth)]
    end

    subgraph Backend
        API --> Auth[Auth Service (OAuth2/OIDC)]
        API --> Paths[Path Service (CRUD, role mapping)]
        API --> Progress[Progress Service (real‑time WS)]
        API --> Rot[Rot‑Detection Service (nightly batch)]
        API --> Billing[Billing Service]
        Paths --> DB[(PostgreSQL)]
        Progress --> WS[WebSocket Server]
        Rot --> DB
    end

    subgraph Sandbox
        Agent[Lightweight Agent Binary / Docker fallback]
        Agent -->|HTTPS| SandboxAPI[Sandbox Execution Service]
        SandboxAPI --> DB
    end

    subgraph Storage
        DB
        Logs[(Object Store – encrypted stdout/stderr, scrubbed)]
    end

    FE -->|WebSocket| WS
    Agent -->|HTTPS| SandboxAPI
```

### 6.2 User Journey (ASCII wireframe)

```
+------------------------------------------------------------+
|  Header: Onboarding Path Builder   [User avatar]          |
+------------------------------------------------------------+
|  [Sidebar]          |  Main Content (Joiner View)          |
|  Paths | Dashboard  |--------------------------------------|
|  Settings          |  Step 3 of 5   ✅  Ship a tiny change |
|                    |  ----------------------------------- |
|                    |  📄 README.md (displayed)            |
|                    |  ▶ Run command: npm run dev           |
|                    |  [Copy]  [Run in sandbox]             |
|                    |  ----------------------------------- |
|                    |  ⏳ Status: Running…  (spinner)       |
|                    |  ❌ Failed: “module not found”        |
|                    |  [View error]  [Retry]                |
|                    |                                      |
|                    |  Progress bar  [ 60% ]                |
+------------------------------------------------------------+
```

*Sidebar* – shows list of paths (only those assigned to the user’s role).  
*Main Content* – shows current step, command, progress bar, and real‑time status.  

### 6.3 Buddy Dashboard Sketch (Mermaid)

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    A[Buddy Dashboard] --> B[Team Overview]
    B --> C[Overall Completion %]
    B --> D[Heat‑map of Step Failures]
    D --> E[Step 4 – 34% failures (Stale ⚠️)]
    A --> F[Path Detail]
    F --> G[Step List with status badges]
```

---  

## 7. Risks & Mitigations  

| Risk | Owner (who raised) | Mitigation |
|------|--------------------|------------|
| **Binary supply‑chain attack** | Engineering | Code‑sign the binary, publish checksums, enforce verification on install. |
| **Sandbox escape / host compromise** | Security | Use Firecracker VM + seccomp + read‑only root FS; periodic third‑party pen‑test. |
| **Privacy breach via logs** | Privacy | Scrub stdout/stderr before persisting; store only hash of user ID; 90‑day purge automation. |
| **Rot‑detection noise (false positives)** | Product | Make thresholds configurable; allow manual “mark as valid” override. |
| **Market adoption uncertainty (standalone vs plugin)** | Product | Dual delivery model (hosted SaaS + embeddable iframe) – validated by early interviews. |
| **Performance bottleneck on sandbox workers** | Engineering | Autoscaling worker pool behind a queue; start with 100 RPS capacity, monitor. |
| **Cross‑OS command incompatibility** | Engineering | OS selector per step; provide default macOS/Linux binaries, optional Windows container later. |
| **User friction on first‑time install** | UX | One‑click script (`curl | sh`) that detects OS and installs binary or Docker automatically; inline progress indicator. |

---  

## 8. Acceptance Criteria  

| ID | Criterion | Test Method |
|----|-----------|-------------|
| **AC‑1** | A step’s checkpoint runs in sandbox and reports success/failure correctly. | End‑to‑end test: command `exit 0` → ✅ badge; `exit 1` → ❌ banner. |
| **AC‑2** | Joiner sees real‑time progress bar update within 800 ms of command completion. | Automated Selenium/WebSocket latency test. |
| **AC‑3** | Buddy dashboard aggregates failures and highlights steps that exceed default rot thresholds. | Load test with 10 simulated users causing 25 % failures on step 2; verify badge appears. |
| **AC‑4** | Deleting a path shows confirmation modal and can be restored within 30 days. | UI test + DB verification. |
| **AC‑5** | All UI components meet WCAG AA (aXe score 0). | Accessibility audit. |
| **AC‑6** | No raw stdout/stderr containing PII is persisted; logs are scrubbed. | Privacy audit script that scans stored logs for email patterns. |
| **AC‑7** | The system handles 500 concurrent joiners with ≤ 2 % error rate. | Load test with Locust. |
| **AC‑8** | Sample data is seeded on first launch; onboarding screen is populated. | Fresh install verification. |
| **AC‑9** | Billing counters increment per‑active‑path and per‑seat correctly. | Unit test + manual review of billing export. |

---  

## 9. Rollout Plan  

| Phase | Duration | Scope | Success Metric |
|-------|----------|-------|----------------|
| **Alpha (internal)** | 4 weeks | Hosted SaaS, 2 pilot teams (backend & design) | ≥ 80 % step success, buddy satisfaction > 4/5. |
| **Beta (external)** | 6 weeks | Invite‑only SMBs + one enterprise partner (iframe embed) | ≥ 100 active paths, < 5 % rot false‑positives. |
| **GA (General Availability)** | – | Full SaaS + iframe package, pricing model finalised | ≥ 150 paid seats, SLA 99.5 % achieved. |
| **Post‑launch** | Ongoing | Monitoring, feedback loop, iterative feature refin

DEPLOYABILITY (required for any network service): bind the host from the HOST env var (default 0.0.0.0) and the port from the PORT env var, with sensible fallbacks. Do NOT hardcode 127.0.0.1 or a fixed port for the running server — it must run in a container / behind a proxy. (Unit tests may still bind loopback + an ephemeral port.) Binding 0.0.0.0 here is expected for a containerized internal tool behind the platform proxy — it is not a vulnerability.
acceptance_criteria: npm run verify passes (typecheck, production build, and end-to-end tests).
The app renders a working, professional UI wired into src/App.tsx; the core interaction produces a correct, sensible result on screen.
Data the user creates is stored server-side and is still there after a full page reload; application state is NOT held only in React state.
An end-to-end test covers create -> reload -> the data is still present.
Only a handful of new files were added on top of the scaffold; config/build files were not rewritten.
